texts.facts: 1. This is a criminal revision petition u/s 397/399 Cr.P.C. filed against order dated 24.02.2021 passed by the court of Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate (NI Act), Digital Court-02/SED in Criminal Complaint No. 526/2021 titled as IFCI Factors Limited Through Authorized Representative Vs. Critical Mass Multilink Ltd., whereby the revisionist and some others were summoned to face trial for the commission of offence punishable u/s 138 Negotiable Instruments Act (hereinafter referred to NI Act). The said complaint was made by respondent herein. For the sake of convenience, the respondent shall be referred to as "complainant" hereinafter. Brief Facts 2. Briefly stated, the case put forth by the complainant against the revisionist and others (including a company namely Critical Mass Multilink Ltd.) in the said complaint is that the cheques issued by the said company in its favour were dishonoured upon presentation. The said company and its Directors were served a legal notice demanding the payment due under the said cheques, but no response was received. Consequently, the above mentioned complaint was filed against the said company as well as its Directors including the revisionist. Grounds of Revision Crl. Revision No: 404/2024 Pawan Kumar Agrawal Vs. IFCI Factors Ltd. page no. 2 of 21 3. The grounds cited by the revisionist are as under:- A. Because the Ld. MM has failed to consider the fact that the petitioner was never a Director of the Critical Mass Multilink Ltd at the relevant time, when the alleged cheque dated 18.11.2020 was presented by the IFCI Factors Ltd company, as the petitioner had already resigned from Critical Mass Multilink Ltd vide resignation dated 22.11.2017, and the same was accepted by the Critical Mass Multilink. Therefore the petitioner herein is not liable to be proceeded against under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and the summoning order and the complaint filed by respondent is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] order on this ground alone. B. Because the Ld. MM has failed to consider that if the offence under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 is by a Company then in that case principles of Section 141 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 have to be followed and as per Section 141 in case of offence by Company only those persons who are in charge of the Company or who conduct the business of the Company are liable for the Acts of the company and ora liable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. Therefore applying the above test it is very clear that since the petitioner had resigned from the Company on Crl. Revision No: 404/2024 Pawan Kumar Agrawal Vs. IFCI Factors Ltd. page no. 3 of 21 22.11.2017 and the cheque has been presented / dishonour on 20.11.2020 i.e. after almost more than three year of the resignation of the petitioner, then since the petitioner was not in charge of the business of the Critical Mass Multilink ltd Company, he cannot be proceeded against under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. Therefore the summoning order and the complaint filed by respondent is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] qua the petitioner. Therefore the summoning order and the complaint filed by respondent is liable to be discharged qua the petitioner.
